newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER CONFIRM NAPOLI'S SIMONI AS NEW COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER CONFIRM NAPOLI'S SIMONI AS NEW COACH.

text.p: Napoli's Luigi Simoni will take over from Roy Hodgson as Internazionale coach next season, the Milan club's president Massimo Moratti confirmed on Friday.
Moratti said he did not know yet whether England midfielder Paul Ince would be staying.
Simoni's appointment has been taken for granted in Italy after he announced last month he would be leaving Napoli, although neither side have openly confirmed a deal.

"Simoni is not taking over a side that needs rebuilding but an Inter that needs an important acquisition in every sector to be title-winning," Moratti said. "I have met Simoni few times but I liked him immediately."
The president said many of the club's plans were on hold until England international Ince, who has become a key figure in midfield, made his mind up about his future.
"I don't know if he will stay, maybe after the cup match his future could become clearer," said Moratti.
Inter play a UEFA Cup semifinal second leg against Monaco of France on Tuesday after winning the home leg 3-1.
"If he stays I will be really happy but if he wants to return to England I will understand because I know he has good reasons," he added.
Ince has been linked to several English clubs, notably Arsenal. His wife is expecting their second child and newspapers have said that she was keen to return home.
Moratti said Inter were looking at PSV Eindhoven midfielder Philip Cocu.
"We are following him and are in a position to take him but Simoni does not know him," he said.
